steps.name: Define significant gene list and background universe from DE results
caveats: Use the full 12000-gene tested panel (not a generic genome-wide list) as the ORA background, since that is the actual universe that could have been called significant

sample_01 has ~4x below-median library size; this is a caveat of the upstream DE call already reflected in de_results.csv and is not re-analyzed here — note it in output as an inherited QC caveat, do not attempt to redo DESeq2
steps.question: Which genes in the treated (AD lesional) vs control DESeq2 contrast meet significance thresholds, and what is the correct background gene universe for a GO over-representation test?
acceptance_criteria: Reads de_results.csv (12000 x 8: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2fc SE/stat/pvalue/padj columns) and metadata.csv

Applies a documented significance cutoff (padj < 0.05, |log2FoldChange| > 1 as default, both stated explicitly in output) and reports the resulting number of significant genes up- and down-regulated separately
Writes out three gene lists as plain gene-symbol text/CSV: significant genes (all), background universe (all 12000 tested genes with non-NA padj), and optionally up/down subsets
Reports how many gene symbols in de_results.csv fail to map to standard HGNC symbols (if any) so the downstream ORA step knows the effective queryable set

steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation analysis
caveats: GO BP is a deeply nested ontology; do not report raw term counts as if they were independent discoveries — state redundancy handling in the summary
If the significant gene list is very small (e.g., <10-15 genes), note that ORA power is limited and results should be read as exploratory
steps.question: Which GO Biological Process terms are significantly over-represented among the genes significant in the AD lesional vs control contrast, relative to the 12000-gene tested background?
acceptance_criteria: Runs a hypergeometric/Fisher's exact ORA (e.g., via clusterProfiler::enricher or gseapy enrich) of the significant gene list against GO Biological Process gene sets, using the study's own 12000-gene tested panel as the background universe (not the default whole-genome background)
Uses the human GO:BP gene set collection staged in the reference store (MSigDB C5 GO:BP, HGNC symbols, GOBP_* set names) — reports if it is absent and cannot proceed without substitution
Reports term name, gene ratio, background ratio, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value (FDR), and the overlapping gene symbols for every term passing FDR < 0.05

Explicitly addresses GO hierarchy redundancy: collapses or flags parent/child terms sharing >=80% of their significant overlapping genes, so the final table is not dozens of near-duplicate entries from the same pathway block
Produces a ranked results table (CSV) and a summary bar/dot plot of the top enriched terms by FDR

plan.title: GO BP over-representation, AD lesional vs control DE genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The de_results.csv already carries a DESeq2 treated-vs-control (AD lesional vs control) contrast for 12000 genes across 6 vs 6 skin samples. The research question is purely about which GO biological processes are over-represented among the genes that came out significant in that contrast — an over-representation analysis (ORA) task, not a re-run of differential expression. The plan therefore has one preparatory step (define the significant gene list and the appropriate background/universe from the existing DE table) and one ORA step (hypergeometric/Fisher test of that list against GO Biological Process gene sets, using the whole 12000-gene panel as background rather than a generic genome-wide background, since the assay only measured those genes). The human MSigDB C5 GO:BP GMT staged in the reference store is used as the gene-set resource — it is species-matched (Homo sapiens) and is the canonical GO BP source. Because GO is a nested hierarchy, the enrichment step must flag redundancy among significant terms rather than reporting a flat list. The known low-library-size outlier (sample_01) is a caveat for the original DE call, not something this ORA step re-litigates, since a finished, presumably QC'd DE table was handed off as the analysis input.
